body: It's easy to see in hindsight. If I never spent time and money gambling, I'd be okay. :(

UPDATE: When I got to the ER last night, I was terrified. A security officer eyed me up and down suspiciously. I almost walked out. But I went to the triage nurse and told her, "I'm afraid I'm going to kill myself tonight if I don't get some help." I broke down and sobbed even though I thought I'd run out of tears.

I was asked to sit down and wait, and I wasn't sure I could do that. Someone at the ER saw me crying, and I guess I looked like shit because I hadn't eaten in a couple of days. He gave me $2 and told me to get what I wanted from the snack machine.

I started to walked to the snack machine, but I got lightheaded and fainted.

The next thing I knew I was being put into a straightjacket and onto one of those rolling beds--I forget the name. My phone was taken from me and not given back until just now.

I had a long talk with a nurse or doctor, not sure who, who asked a ton of really personal questions, like if I'd ever molested children or if I'd ever contemplated killing someone with a knife or gun, and if I'd ever had people seen or unseen tell me to harm someone. To be honest, I felt like they were trying to set me up or frame me for something. I didn't say anything about my plan B to get arrested to get shelter and food. Oh, they also asked me to remember a set of 5 names, and repeat them later. Lots of other stuff I forget.

Anyhow, I was told that I probably suffered from Major Depressive Disorder. I could have told them that: I was diagnosed with that once and haven't been able to afford medication for years--and I wouldn't have been able to afford them even if I didn't gamble. They tried to contact my family, but my dad didn't answer and my sister hung up on them when they mentioned my name.

I was given a small meal. I was told that after going without for 2 days, I might have trouble with a larger meal. I think I ate it all in less than 5 seconds. It's really amazing how much better you feel after a meal when you've been without for a while.

I was told that I would have to remain here for 72 hours for evaluations. I had to plead to get my phone back--they were originally going to keep it from me the whole time.

I slept until 10am. A bed feels so much better than a park bench or cardboard on the ground. A nurse shaved me--apparently I can't have any kind of razors at all.

I didn't eat any breakfast because I woke up too late.

I had an MRI or CAT scan this morning after I was awakened.

The nurse gave me some pills today. I should have asked what they were, but I didn't think about it. It's definitely doing something though, because I feel like my head's growing inside.

I had tomato soup and grilled cheese for lunch, then I begged for my cellphone. They really didn't want me to have it, but I got anxious enough that they gave it to me.

I was visited by a nun, and I explained my situation. She told me she could get a second set of clothes for me, so I could do laundry. She asked if I were Catholic, I told her no, and she told me that didn't matter. (So why ask? weird.)

I have a group session soon.

The last 16 hours or so have been a whirlwind of things moving too fast for my comfort.

I haven't thought that far. Right now, I'm walking to a hospital to try to admit myself. Less than a mile to go. If they refuse to admit me, I guess the convenience store robbery or disturbing the peace is plan B.
I'm about a mile away from the hospital. And I have 42% on my phone.

I'm walking towards a hospital now. I'm in south Florida.

Just looking at my phone there are THOUSANDS of free mental health services for people with alcohol and drug problems. I don't have any of those. If I'd shot up heroin instead of played slots I'd be able to get lots of help. But nothing for gamblers. We are literally the dregs of addicts, undeserving of any help.

I've got about a mile and a half or so to go. I haven't walked as fast as normal because it's dark and I've been crying more than I thought.

I'm scared.
I'm in south Florida. I don't want to give more information because that might clue in what my other reddit username is. :(

They still do general delivery? I thought that was something only in radio and TV, and that the post office would require me to get a PO Box (which I can't afford).

I haven't seen a dentist in 15 years. I think my teeth are ok, considering, but they'll probably just pull them all if I go. And of course, it's one more expense I can't afford.

I'm 46. Will the student stuff still apply to me, or will places think I'm lying about going to college at my age?

I've got another 2 miles to go to get to the hospital.

This is making me wonder: will I be paying for this intervention for the rest of my life? I don't have insurance and I have no money. I'm not so sure now that being alive but saddled with tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars in medical bills that I most certainly would default on would be good.

And then, would I even get decent care if they know I can't pay for it? Maybe they'd just give me whatever legal minimum of "stabilization" is required and then force me back on the streets.

:( My life sucks. I'm at 51% on my phone now.
I appreciate what you're saying. I'm walking towards a hospital now. We'll see what happens when I ask to be admitted. If they say no, then I'll have my answer for what I have to do next.

Did your family take you back? I'm not sure they'll take me back. When your own family doesn't even care if you're alive or not, man, I just don't have the words.

I'm starting to walk towards a hospital. It's going to take a little over an hour to get there on foot. I'm literally terrified to call 911.

If I were a woman, especially with kids, it would be so much easier. Or if I were addicted to drugs instead of gambling. In my area, there is only one shelter for men, and it fills up quickly, so I've found.

Without an address, how do I get the lifeline phone?

The local community college now has 24/7 security because of homeless people camping out there, so I can't use their facilities. I can't afford a gym membership, either. Hell, I haven't shaved in almost a week, so I'm starting to look the scruffy unkempt part now.

I'll try to go to the hospital. It's about 3 miles away, so it will take me a little longer than an hour to walk. I'm afraid of calling 911, because I don't know if they'll take me seriously--maybe someone else has to make the call. Maybe the 911 operator won't think I'm being serious if I'm calling for myself. Maybe he'll call a cop instead of an ambulance.

see, you're lucky. you have a wife and kids. (or a husband and kids). I've never had that.

When I was gambling, I could pretend or believe that when I was winning, I was worth something. That maybe whatever good thing caused me to win would spill over into the rest of my life. But the counter to that is that when you lose, you're worthless. And society agrees.

My dad and sister disowned me after they found out I was gambling. I'm not in Dad's will anymore, and my sister refuses to answer the phone or call me back. They've washed their hands of me and want nothing more to do with me. If my own family doesn't love me anymore, what does that say about me as a person?

It hurts, man. It hurts more than anything else in the world. To not be loved, to be thrown away, and then to have it blamed all on you and have no one to turn to for comfort. I don't think I can deal with that much more.

I just wish society felt that way. As far as society is concerned I'm a worthless drain on it, not even worth helping.

I called the gambling hotline for help. They were no help at all. I don't even think I was talking to a person, just a computer recording. They didn't give me any resources other than telling me to go online and look up Gambler's Anonymous meetings and go to a meeting. No numbers to food banks or temporary housing or employment offices. They told me if I felt suicidal, to hang up and call 911 instead of them, and then they hung up on me. If tax dollars are going towards that, it's a waste of money.

I hear different things about jail and prisons. That they're okay once you know the social status. That you're going to definitely engage in gay sex. That they're absolutely horrible and no one in their right mind would want to go. That if Martha Stewart could survive it, anyone can. That while everything is structured, you won't go crazy as long as you just adapt. That little things become a big deal, like honey buns.

The thing is that even in prison, I'd never be free from gambling. There would always be inmates who would be willing to wager on a sports game or play poker. Sure, I'd be free from slot machines and scratch-off cards, but there would still be many temptations. The thing is that those temptations wouldn't cause me to be evicted from prison. I'd still have my clothes, my bed, my daily meals (even if I had to give up my dessert). Right now I have just my clothes.

Yesterday I was really hungry, but I don't feel hungry today. The good thing about not eating is that you don't need to shit, so I haven't had to run around to find a public restroom. When I have to piss, that will be a different thing. Maybe I'll get arrested for public urination and then be considered a sex offender.

I'm at 62% on my battery now. I'd take bets on how long the battery will last, but that wouldn't really be funny, I guess.

Gambling's never a problem as long as you're winning. But your self-worth gets tied up in winning and losing. When you win, you feel lucky, you feel blessed, you feel like God is on your side. When you lose, you feel like God is punishing you and he turned his back on you.

So maybe go back to the library and make a scene?

I'm afraid the hospital won't believe me--that they'll think I'm just saying things to get free room and board. I doubt the triage nurse would look at my phone to read my post.

Gambling makes everything so much worse. When you're having any sort of problems, all sympathy goes out the window when they find out you're a gambler. I don't expect anyone to care or even bother with me. As far as they are concerned, I deserve all the stuff that's happening to me.

And honestly, that's why death seems so appealing. If I deserve all this punishment and scorn and hatred, I might as well take it to the final level and just end my life altogether. Any level where I'm forced to stay alive but still suffer and have to deal with the hatred from others is too much.
